verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {petitioner_name}, the Petitioner herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above petition are true and correct to my personal knowledge and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Petitioner

promptInstructions: Draft a Writ Petition (Civil) under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
Cause-title MUST include three-tier 'In the matter of' format: (1) Article 226, (2) the statute involved, (3) grievance summary, (4) parties.
Para 1: Description of parties — petitioner with full particulars; respondents in hierarchical order (Union > State > authority > private respondents).
Para 2: Jurisdiction under Article 226(2) — cause of action wholly or in part arose within this HC's territory OR respondent authority located within territory.
Para 3-6: Statement of facts in chronological order.
Para 7: Impugned order / action / inaction — date, issuing authority, content. Annex copy.
Para 8: Locus standi — petitioner's legal injury / fundamental right / statutory right affected.

Para 9: Alternative remedy — Cite Whirlpool Corporation v. Registrar of Trade Marks (1998) 8 SCC 1 — alternative remedy not absolute bar; exceptions: (i) violation of fundamental right, (ii) violation of natural justice, (iii) order without jurisdiction, (iv) vires challenge.

Para 10: Grounds — numbered (A), (B), (C)... constitutional grounds (Article 14 arbitrariness, Article 19 unreasonable restriction, Article 21 procedure not just/fair/reasonable per Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) 1 SCC 248, Article 300A property without authority of law); statutory grounds (ultra vires the statute, contrary to statutory mandate, non-application of mind, mala fides, irrelevant considerations, Wednesbury unreasonableness).
Doctrine of legitimate expectation — Cite Food Corporation of India v. Kamdhenu Cattle Feed (1993) 1 SCC 71; Navjyoti Co-operative v. Union of India (1992) 4 SCC 477.
Doctrine of proportionality — Cite Om Kumar v. Union of India (2001) 2 SCC 386.
Where action affects livelihood / human dignity, cite Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984) 3 SCC 161; Olga Tellis v. BMC (1985) 3 SCC 545.

Where service matter — Cite State of UP v. Mohd Nooh AIR 1958 SC 86 (HC writ over service tribunals); B.C. Chaturvedi v. Union of India (1995) 6 SCC 749 (scope of judicial review in service matters — limited to procedural infirmity, mala fides, perversity).
Where regulatory order challenged — Cite Reliance Energy Ltd v. Maharashtra State Road Development Corp (2007) 8 SCC 1 (judicial review in commercial matters limited).
Para 11: Interim relief — stay of impugned order / status quo; balance of convenience and irreparable injury.

Para 12: Limitation / laches — no statutory limitation for Art. 226, but unreasonable delay defeats relief — Cite Tilokchand Motichand v. H.B. Munshi (1969) 1 SCC 110; State of MP v. Bhailal Bhai AIR 1964 SC 1006 (3 years as guide for monetary claims).
Prayer must specify writ type (mandamus / certiorari / prohibition / quo warranto) and consequential reliefs.
Affidavit in support is mandatory under HC Writ Rules (e.g., Allahabad HC Rules Chapter XXII; Delhi HC Rules; Patna HC Writ Rules; Jharkhand HC Rules).
Court fee per state HC fees schedule.
Append Lawie disclaimer at end.

sections.description: Equality before law and equal protection of laws
Protection of life and personal liberty — Maneka Gandhi expanded scope
Power of HC to issue writs (broader than Art. 32 — also for legal rights, not only FR)
Power of superintendence over courts and tribunals
No deprivation of property except by authority of law

filing_checklist: Certified / true copy of impugned order
Representations made to authority + replies (showing exhaustion of departmental remedy where applicable)
Documents proving cause of action territorial nexus
Court fee per HC fee schedule
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: respondents_list must include at least one respondent and full address
writ_type must have at least one option selected
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
Court level restricted to High Court only

Whirlpool Corp v. Registrar of Trade Marks (1998) 8 SCC 1 — Alternative remedy exceptions
Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984) 3 SCC 161 — Right to live with dignity
Olga Tellis v. BMC (1985) 3 SCC 545 — Right to livelihood under Art. 21
Tilokchand Motichand v. H.B. Munshi (1969) 1 SCC 110 — Laches in writ
State of MP v. Bhailal Bhai AIR 1964 SC 1006 — Limitation as guide
B.C. Chaturvedi v. Union of India (1995) 6 SCC 749 — Service matter judicial review
Food Corp of India v. Kamdhenu Cattle Feed (1993) 1 SCC 71 — Legitimate expectation
